The whole `docs/evidence` tree has moved on as well, since later sets landed, which is why the set-level identity above rather than a whole-tree one is the fact to re-check. The pre-squash spelling `637da5b07b5d5b1519768e8f9306c9a97c8dcd4a` is reachable from no ref and dies at the next gc, which is why it is no longer cited; this is a change of citation and not of content.

countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 824 at this head, and the assertion is the definition rather than a restatement of it: 974 `.webp` are committed and the 20 `supplementary` sets below account for 150 of them (one of those sets declares no frames), leaving 824. Re-derived for THIS tree and stated once. The two sides had each written their own figure and neither survives: this branch's 824 was counted at its 942-frame tree (18 sets, 118 declared) and `main`'s 740 at its 886-frame tree (19 sets, 146 declared, after `#139` added `new-chat-row`), and the merged tree is the UNION of both frame sets - this branch's 942 committed frames plus `main`'s thirty-two, the sixteen `clear-search/` frames `#136` added and the sixteen `new-chat-row/` frames `#139` added, 974 in all - so the figure here is counted off the disk and the summed declared frames rather than added from either side's field. Superseded derivations are deleted rather than quoted, on the rule this field already carried: a stale derivation is worse here than none, because the field's whole justification is that a reader can re-compute it, and one that does not resolve teaches them to stop checking. The three terms above are the whole arithmetic, they are read from the tree rather than transcribed (`find docs/evidence -name '*.webp' | wc -l`, and the summed `frames` of the sets below), and `check-evidence.mjs` fails when they disagree with it. This branch carries no version bump of its own: it is rebased and merged up rather than merged with a bump, so `package.json` on it reads whatever the base it was last synced to carries (`0.20.1`), and no resolution along the way touched the version line - which is what the repository's version-bump guard reads.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 115 entries, counted off the merged literal by the gate itself rather than summed from the two sides (102 on this branch before the rebase, 108 on `main`, each written by a run taken before the other side landed - which is exactly why the merged figure is counted and not added: 115 = 108 + the seven stories this branch registers that `main` does not - `canvas-workspace--files-scanning`, `--files-scan-stopped`, `--files-scan-stopped-empty`, `--pdf-viewer`, `--image-viewer`, `--audio-viewer`, `--video-viewer`). The gate counts the list and fails a mismatch, so this field cannot silently lag its own source.

partialCapture.note: REBASE RE-STAMP onto `c0570ea60` (`main`, 0.19.7 plus #118, #136, #137 and #138) - the third rebase this branch has carried, and the first whose re-stamp is NOT accompanied by a re-capture. That is a decision about the delta rather than about the cost: the two earlier rebases landed packaging and docs, and were re-captured so the tree hashes would rest on a run rather than on an argument, while what lands here is one renderer change - #136's clear control inside the sidebar's search field (`chat-sidebar.tsx`, the new `clear-search.ts`) - whose only painted difference is the control itself plus the `pr-9` that reserves its column, and both sit behind the `{query && ...}` guard, so a frame of that field with an empty query is the same frame before and after. That is measured in the tree rather than only argued: `clear-search/before-rest` and `clear-search/after-rest` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in both themes, the same empty-query sidebar painted by the pre-change tree and by the post-change tree, which is #136's own readback. So the only frames whose state is different are the ones that paint a non-empty query, and the only set that does is `clear-search` itself, taken on the changed tree. The sweep cannot paint the sidebar at all - its `STORIES` list holds nothing that renders it - so the sets that carry it besides `clear-search` are `chat-title` and `sidebar-new-chat`, whose 38 frames across both themes all draw the empty placeholder with no clear control (looked at, not inferred), and `model-picker-feedback`, whose frames show the field empty behind its scrim; no other set in the tree is about that field at all - `clear-search`'s own README and readbacks are the only evidence in the tree that names it - and `mentioned-files-app` is cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect and carries no sidebar. `provenanceNote` states the same finding from the tree side, in its strongest form: 0 `.webp` differ between the head the last pass ran at and this one, so no re-capture could have produced a different file. `refreshedFromHead` is the head every run of that pass was taken at, cited as its replay here, and `addedAtHead`/`refreshedAtHead` move with it. No frame was added, removed or rewritten by this rebase, so `addedFrames` 12 and `addedSurfaces` still name the round-2 pass that added them, and the pass's own figures below are the ones it measured. Re-POINTED: while the branch ref existed these three citations were spelled with branch commits (`a9ed72ad7a9ab78f05614cddd70e088cc1029d21` for `addedAtHead`, `637da5b07b5d5b1519768e8f9306c9a97c8dcd4a` for both refreshes); #128 was squash-merged and the branch deleted, so none of them is reachable from a ref any more and each is cited as its reachable spelling on `main` - `e8ebe5c6d189ed07dc69515e351d9576b35a8d6d`, whose `src` tree is byte-identical to `main`'s (its `scripts` tree is the one this file recorded, re-stamped for the current tree in `scriptsTree` above). Which run the frames came from is unchanged; only the spelling that survives a gc is. Pointing `refreshedFromHead` at the merge commit rather than at a branch spelling is deliberate: the gate reads it as `passStart` and counts committed `.webp` against `refreshedFrames`, and over the wider window that count is 96 against the 108 claimed, so the check fails closed rather than opening. Twelve frames of headroom is thin and grows as later evidence lands, so anyone re-pointing this again should re-measure the count rather than assume the margin.

THE REBASE, and the first one here that re-stamps without re-capturing. `main` moved three times under this branch during the round - to `e4d074c60` (0.19.6), to `98c32e85e` (0.19.7 plus #138, which the previous pass re-captured at), and then to `c0570ea60` (0.19.7 plus #136). That move is not packaging: it adds `src/renderer/src/features/chat/clear-search.ts` and rewrites the search field in `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-sidebar.tsx` (+51/-8), so `srcTree` moved for the first time in any of these rebases, and `scripts/` moved with it (`scripts/clear-search.test.mjs`). A stamp whose tree has moved is exactly the case the earlier passes answered by re-capturing; this one answered it with two facts about the frames. The first is the shape of the change: it paints a clear control INSIDE the field and only while the query is non-empty (the `{query && ...}` guard around the button in `chat-sidebar.tsx`), plus a `pr-9` on the input that reserves the control's column and a `my-2` moved from the input onto a `relative` wrapper around it, which reproduces the same box - so with an empty query the field renders the same placeholder, the same border and the same box as it did before. The second is the measurement that closes it: `clear-search/before-rest` and `clear-search/after-rest` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in both themes, the same empty-query sidebar painted once on the pre-change tree and once on the post-change tree, so nothing in that state depends on #136 at all. Every frame in this tree of that state is therefore unchanged, and the only frames whose state differs are the non-empty-query ones, all of them in `clear-search` itself, which were taken on the changed tree by #136. The sets that carry the field besides `clear-search` were looked at rather than assumed to be empty: `chat-title` and `sidebar-new-chat` draw the empty placeholder with no clear control in all 38 of their frames across both themes, `model-picker-feedback` shows the same empty field behind its scrim, and `mentioned-files-app` is cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect and carries no sidebar at all; no other set in the tree is about that field - `clear-search`'s own README and readbacks are the only evidence in the tree that names it. Nothing else in the tree was a different source for these pixels either, and that is measurable in the same way: 0 `.webp` differ between the head the previous pass ran at (`98b827108`, orphaned by the force-push that carried this re-stamp) and this head.

THE SYNC MERGE, and what it does and does not claim about the frames. `main` moved three times more - to `6f9bc2d04` (#140: the desktop toolchain, Electron 44 and TypeScript 7), to `4ffc3f2b5` (#139: the New chat row aligned with All chats, without the pill) and to `ad09ec6b4` (the 0.20.1 release) - and this branch was merged up onto it rather than replayed onto it, because a rebase would rewrite all twenty-two commits and orphan every citation this manifest carries while changing no pixel a reader can see. Two paths conflicted: `package.json` (resolved the same way as before - `main`'s `version` line, now 0.20.1, with the UNION of the two sides' `test:desktop` lists, which now carry all three of the test files the sides added, this branch's `mentioned-files.test.mjs` and `main`'s `new-chat-row.test.mjs` and `new-chat-row-evidence.test.mjs`) and this manifest's stamp block, where two re-stamps had to be reconciled; `src/main/index.ts` was auto-merged, both sides' hunks kept. No frame was re-taken for the merge, and the two upstream changes are treated differently for a reason. #140 moves the toolchain (`package.json`, `electron.vite.config.js`, the `tsconfig`s, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, three `scripts/` files, five `src/main/` modules and one renderer component) and not the canvas, the mentioned-files producer or the sidebar, and `main` itself did not re-sweep for it: it re-stamped its trees and committed the toolchain set's own packaged frame beside the swept ones, which is the same position this branch takes for the frames it contributed. #139 does move the sidebar's New chat row, and the three sets that photograph the sidebar (`chat-title`, `sidebar-new-chat` and `model-picker-feedback`'s scrimmed background) predate it: they are pictures of the sidebar as it stood at the heads their `capturedAtHead` fields name, this manifest makes no claim that they show the post-#139 row, and `main` carries that change's own before/after evidence beside them in the `new-chat-row` set - which is why the merge adds that set rather than re-driving those older frames. Nothing on either side of the merge touches this branch's own contribution: the canvas surfaces and `mentioned-files-app` are cropped to panels that #139 and #140 do not paint.

This rebase's re-capture found the COUNTS half of the same rule still open - it is a zero-add pass, and `main`'s accumulating writer reset them to 0/[] anyway, which is what these two values were corrected from - so the writer now leaves the whole added-pass record alone unless a run actually adds frames. unchangedControl.why: The honesty check for this pass, and the reason a moved frame is legible as one: a surface this rebase does not paint differently was re-captured through the same command, on the same host, in the same session as the nine it does. All twelve came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the encoder and the renderer are deterministic here at this load. The class the moved frames belong to was measured the same way in the previous pass, which ran `audio-viewer` twice: its `neon` frame - which moved in the first run of BOTH passes - came back exactly the committed bytes in that second run. Neither control separates the widget from the encoder for `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, whose difference is the platform PDF plugin not painting at all and which reproduced byte-for-byte instead (see `recaptureNote`).

partialCapture.recaptureNote: Re-captured in place, at the rebased head, and the result is one-sided: 101 of the 108 frames came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed bytes, and all 48 of the four Files surfaces plus all 12 control frames are among them. The 7 that moved are media-viewer frames - pdf 1 (`localOperatorDark`), image 2 (`synth`, `radient`), audio 2 (`neon`, `radient`), video 2 (`synth`, `radient`) - and six of the seven moved only at the lossy encoder's own quantisation scale: at an 8% tolerance (20/255) ZERO pixels differ, and the worst RMSE is 0.00054 (`video-viewer/radient`, 4,342 px of 1,152,000). That class is established rather than assumed: the same command on the same tree was run twice in the previous pass, and `audio-viewer/neon` - which moved in both passes' first runs - came back EXACTLY the committed bytes in one of them, so the movement is the widget repaint and the encoder and a frame that has moved is not read as a change unless it survives a second run. The seventh, `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, is a reproducible platform paint failure and not that class: this session's private headless Chrome never painted the PDF guest document - a probe at 640,200 reads the platform field `srgb(40,40,40)` where the committed frame reads the white page - with a byte-for-byte identical difference (204,364 px, 163,673 of them above 8%) in both passes. The viewer's own source (`pdf-preview.tsx`, `canvas-file-viewer.tsx`, the story) is untouched by `main`'s move, and this branch's canvas hunks in `chat-page.tsx` and `chat-content.tsx` - the one host surface the rebase had to carry - survive line-for-line, so the committed frame is the one that depicts the surface under review; it is retained and NO byte-identity claim is made for it. The 7 frames whose committed bytes are retained are the same picture the re-capture measured.
